title: Client retention KPI dimension matrix and measurement digest
content:
Purpose and shape
------------------
This short digest is intended for Customer Success (CS) and Account teams prepping QBRs and renewal conversations. It focuses on four operational KPI dimensions we repeatedly see drive renewal conversations: latency, uptime, cost-per-token (economics), and cache hit rate.

High-level goals
- Provide precise, reproducible measurement definitions for QBR slides and renewal trackers.
- Offer pragmatic targets by customer tier and a minimal sample KPI table for quick copy/paste.
- Highlight instrumentation notes so CS asks precise questions and engineering can reproduce numbers.

Metric definitions (concise, unambiguous)
------------------------------------------------
1) Latency (two flavors)
- End-to-end latency: time from server-received timestamp (API gateway) to final response byte delivered to the client, measured in milliseconds. Report p50/p95/p99 for the 30-day trailing window and the last 24 hours for recent regressions.
- Model-only latency: time in the inference runtime between request dispatch to model shard and last token generation (excludes network/muxing). Use this for engineering optimizations and to compare model variants.
- Notes: For streamed responses, report both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-last-byte (TTLB). When multiple model variants are in use, show per-variant p95 and the weighted p95 by traffic share.
- Formula (example): p95_end2end_ms = 95th percentile of { end_time_ms - recv_time_ms } across sampled requests in window.

2) Uptime (customer-facing SLA translation)
- Definition: Uptime = 1 - (total_failed_requests / total_valid_requests) in a day, expressed as a percentage. A failed request is any request which returns HTTP 5xx, HTTP 429 when over quota is not the customer's fault, or a client-timed-out response above 15s where the platform aborted.
- Measurement window: daily and rolling 30-day. For QBRs use rolling 30-day aggregate and one recent incident summary if applicable.
- SLA mapping: map platform-level uptime to customer impact using an incident taxonomy (partial: degraded latency > SLO, full: timeouts/errors preventing usage).

3) Cost per token (internal economics vs billed)
- Billed cost/token: what the customer sees on their bill (e.g., $0.0006 / token). Use the billing system's aggregated tokens for the billing period.
- Internal unit cost: allocate cloud compute + reserved GPU amortization + egress/storage + caching savings divided by served tokens in the period. Express in cents per 1k tokens to make numbers legible.
- Example calculation: internal_cents_per_1k_tokens = (gpu_hours_cost + infra_overhead + egress_cost - cache_savings) / (total_tokens / 1000).
- Show both numbers on the QBR slide (customer-facing billed rate and a translated internal unit cost for account economics conversations).

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache)
- Definition: Cache hit rate = (#requests with full-response-from-cache) / (total_cacheable_requests). Use a separate metric for partial hits (first N tokens served from cache then model completions) and for complete hits (no model invocation). Report both.
- Measurement details: Only consider requests that meet the cacheability rules (e.g., prompt length <= configured threshold, non-personalized flag set). Exclude requests that were evicted mid-response due to TTL expiry.
- Formula: cache_hit_pct = 100 * completions_served_entirely_from_cache / cacheable_requests

Minimal KPI table (copy into QBR slide or renewal tracker)
---------------------------------------------------------
Tier | p95 latency (ms) | Rolling 30d uptime | Target cost (cents per 1k tokens) | Cache hit target (%)
-----|------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------
Developer (free) | 450-800 (p95) | 99.0% | 120 c/1k | 10%
Startup | 200-400 (p95) | 99.5% | 60-80 c/1k | 15-25%
Scale / Growth | 120-250 (p95) | 99.8% | 30-50 c/1k | 25-45%
Enterprise | 80-200 (p95) | 99.95% | 10-30 c/1k (reserved) | 40-70%

How to use the table
- Pick the row closest to the account's usage pattern. For customers on Dedicated, show the "Enterprise" column but annotate reserved discounts and committed throughput.
- For Developer-tier customers, emphasize feature/cost tradeoffs (e.g., suggest batching/shorter context windows).

Suggested QBR slide structure (single slide per KPI dimension)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Title: KPI + window (e.g., "p95 end-to-end latency — trailing 30 days")
- Short one-line trend: 30d delta vs prior 30d (e.g., +8% or -32%)
- KPI sparkline (30 days) + histogram of request sizes or token distribution
- Top 3 contributors to the metric change (eg. model rollout, traffic spike, infra upgrade)
- Action items and owner (engineering/CS) with timelines

Instrumentation checklist (quick for engineers)
------------------------------------------------
- Ensure logs include: recv_time_ms, first_byte_ms, last_byte_ms, model_variant, tokens_in_request, cache_status (MISS/PARTIAL/FULL), response_code, route_id.
- Export standardized metrics: latency.p50/p95/p99, uptime.daily, cache.hit_rate.partial/full, token.count.total, internal_cost_per_1k_tokens.
- Tag metrics with customer_id and tier to enable per-account rollups (mask PII).

Presentation notes for renewal conversations
-------------------------------------------
- Start with the customer-facing metrics (p95, 30d uptime) and a short narrative of impact ("Reduced p95 by 180ms, lowering perceived lag on interactive editor").
- Map improved cache hit rate to concrete cost savings (estimate monthly savings = saved_tokens/1000 * internal_cents_per_1k).
- If renewal is at risk: show root causes, mitigations, and a short timeline for engineering fixes. Include a playbook entry to offer temporary credits or dedicated bursts for critical periods.

Quick troubleshooting heuristics (CS + Eng pairing)
--------------------------------------------------
- Latency spike but stable model-only latency: investigate network, ingress autoscaling, or routing mix.
- Model-only spike: look at model variant rollout, sequence-length distribution shifts, or quantization/compatibility issues.
- Uptime drop for a single customer: check per-tenant quota throttles, auth errors, or regional routing fallbacks.

Open questions / items for alignment (actionable)
------------------------------------------------
- Standardize the canonical field names across observability (Chris/RTE team to propose by 2025-01-20).
- Agree on a conservatively defined "cacheable request" boolean produced by the runtime and exposed in logs (CS + Serving runtime to sign off).
- Validate internal_cents_per_1k_tokens calculation for Dedicated customers (finance + infra modeling).

Appendix: quick sample calculation
----------------------------------
- Period: Nov 1–30
- Total tokens served: 4,200,000 tokens
- GPU + infra cost attributed: $2,400
- Egress + storage + other: $600
- Cache savings (model invocations avoided): $300
- internal_cents_per_1k = ((2400 + 600 - 300) / (4,200,000 / 1000)) * 100 = ((2700) / 4200) * 100 = 64.3 cents per 1k tokens

Notes to self (short)
---------------------
- Use this doc as a minimal canonical reference for QBRs.
- Convert this to a one-page cheat sheet for SDRs and AMs.
- Follow up: add example slides + python snippet to compute internal_cents_per_1k in the observability repo.
